method: A second, oppositely oriented quadrupole coil pair with different spatial geometry is superimposed on a standard quadrupole MOT, yielding an octupole-symmetry field whose gradient grows quadratically from zero at the center; D1 and D2 gray-molasses cooling of 41K is characterized by measuring temperature, lifetime, and phase-space density.
result: For both D1 and D2 light the octupole MOT shows longer lifetimes at temperatures comparable to the zero-gradient case, with D1 gray molasses reaching temperatures down to the few-microkelvin range and phase-space densities up to ~10^-? for a modest atom number.
conclusion: The hybrid quadrupole-octupole trap is an effective alternative for continuous sub-Doppler cooling, potentially enabling longer loading times into optical dipole traps for cold-atom experiments.

title: Look Mum, No Hands! Quantum State Preparation Without Time-Dependent Control
authors: Tomasz Andrzejewski, Yuri Minoguchi, Phila Rembold, Konrad Szyma\'nski
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How much can be prepared with a quantum system whose Hamiltonian cannot be modulated in time? Common intuition suggests that the answer is not much. Without a knob to turn during the evolution, a system seems confined to a fixed trajectory through its state space, while time-dependent control can steer it almost anywhere. We put this intuition to the test by studying autonomous control, i.e., state preparation with a time-invariant Hamiltonian, where the only freedom lies in the static coupling strengths and the evolution time. We characterize basic mathematical properties of the autonomously reachable set and introduce two criteria of unreachability: a certificate that is cheap to evaluate and rigorously excludes that a target state can be reached for any choice of control parameters, and a stronger criterion based on exhaustive numerical optimization. With these tools we estimate the probability that a typical state in Hilbert space is unreachable under randomly drawn control terms. The dimensionality of the reachable set turns out to be independent of the system, yet the fraction of Hilbert space lying close to it depends strongly on the choice of control Hamiltonians. Strikingly, for sufficiently random controls and long enough evolution times, almost every state can become approximately reachable, even with the fewest generators that permit full controllability with time-dependent couplings. Autonomous control can approach the expressivity of time-dependent control, at the cost of longer evolution times.
tldr: The paper studies whether arbitrary quantum states can be prepared using a time-invariant Hamiltonian by tuning only static couplings and evolution time.
motivation: It challenges the intuition that without time-dependent control a quantum system is confined to a fixed trajectory and cannot reach most target states.
method: The authors characterize the autonomously reachable set, introduce a cheap unreachability certificate and a stronger numerical-optimization criterion, and estimate the unreachable fraction of Hilbert space for random control Hamiltonians.
result: The reachable set's dimension is system-independent, while the fraction of nearby Hilbert space depends strongly on the chosen controls; with sufficiently random controls and long evolution times, almost every state becomes approximately reachable using minimal generators.
conclusion: Autonomous control can approach the expressivity of time-dependent control, at the cost of longer evolution times.

title: Degree And Normalization Frontiers For Bounded Qsvt Inversion
authors: Hongyu Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) implements matrix inversion using bounded polynomials. Increasing polynomial degree can improve normalization and reduce amplified query cost, with savings that depend on the error criterion. However, existing bounded methods either fix the normalization or work far below the condition numbers of fault-tolerant resource estimates. We therefore analyze this trade-off for absolute reciprocal error, which controls inverse-operator accuracy, and for residual error, which suffices for normalized linear solves. For absolute reciprocal error, we establish a scaling limit to a constrained least-norm problem for entire functions and characterize its high-accuracy frontier using elliptic integrals. Constructions built from near-optimal limiting functions achieve certified query-cost savings over the rescaled minimax baseline of at least 11.8 percent at condition number ten thousand with error one millionth, and at least 22.8 percent at one million with error one ten-billionth. A simpler two-term rule also has certified savings, and its phase factors at condition number ten thousand pass numerical checks at selected points. For residual error, a sparse Chebyshev construction achieves certified savings over the residual-minimax baseline of at least 8.7 percent at condition number ten thousand with normalized-state error at most one hundred-millionth, and at least 13.1 percent at one million with error at most one ten-billionth. These results quantify the saving that a joint choice of degree and normalization gives beyond the minimax baselines.
tldr: The paper analyzes degree-normalization trade-offs for bounded-polynomial QSVT-based matrix inversion under absolute reciprocal and residual error criteria.
motivation: Existing bounded QSVT inversion methods either fix normalization or operate far below condition numbers used in fault-tolerant resource estimates, leaving the degree-normalization trade-off unclear.
method: The authors derive a scaling limit to a constrained least-norm problem for entire functions for absolute reciprocal error, characterize its high-accuracy frontier via elliptic integrals, and also propose sparse Chebyshev constructions for residual error.
result: Certified query-cost savings over rescaled minimax baselines are reported, including at least 11.8% at condition number 10^4 and 22.8% at 10^6 for absolute error, and at least 8.7%/13.1% for residual error at corresponding scales.
conclusion: Jointly choosing polynomial degree and normalization yields quantifiable query-cost improvements beyond standard minimax baselines for QSVT matrix inversion.

title: Parisi Energy Before Parisi Geometry In The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
authors: Bhuvanesh Sundar Maxime Dupont
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The fractured low-energy landscape of spin glasses presents a notorious barrier to optimization. While high-depth calculations indicate that the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can approach the Parisi ground-state energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass, how it does so remains elusive. Here, we treat the QAOA distribution as a statistical-physics object and probe its geometry directly in the thermodynamic limit. We draw two independent bitstrings from the same problem instance and couple them through their macroscopic similarity. We find that typical QAOA samples remain macroscopically uncorrelated, even as their sensitivity to this coupling grows with circuit depth [MATH]. By contrast, the low-energy tail shows a much stronger tendency to overlap and reveals a Parisi-like phase with the same critical behavior as the thermal spin-glass transition. The onset of this organization moves toward the typical output as the circuit deepens, consistent with the separation vanishing only as [MATH]. Together, these findings suggest a route distinct from structure-exploiting classical algorithms and thermal sampling, one in which the QAOA approaches the Parisi energy before Parisi geometry becomes typical.
tldr: The paper analyzes the geometry of QAOA output distributions for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass in the thermodynamic limit and finds a Parisi-like low-energy phase emerging before typical samples develop Parisi geometry.
motivation: Although high-depth QAOA can approach the Parisi ground-state energy of spin glasses, it is unclear how the algorithm organizes its output distribution to achieve this.
method: The authors treat the QAOA distribution as a statistical-physics object, draw pairs of bitstrings from the same instance, couple them via macroscopic similarity, and probe overlap behavior in the thermodynamic limit.
result: Typical QAOA samples remain macroscopically uncorrelated, while the low-energy tail shows stronger overlaps and a Parisi-like phase with critical behavior matching the thermal spin-glass transition.
conclusion: The findings suggest that QAOA approaches the Parisi energy before Parisi geometry becomes typical, indicating a route distinct from structure-exploiting classical algorithms and thermal sampling.

title: QWeaver: Quantum Circuit Cut Workflow With MLIR-based Compiler, Runtime, And Weaver Hybrid Tasks
authors: Narasinga Rao Miniskar, Elaine Wong, Vicente Leyton-Ortega, Sharmin Afrose, Jeffrey S. Vetter, Travis S. Humble
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computers available today are constrained by limited qubit counts and high noise levels, making the direct execution of large quantum circuits infeasible on a single device, and while quantum circuit cutting addresses this by partitioning a large circuit into smaller subcircuits for independent execution, orchestrating the full end-to-end workflow remains a significant programming challenge. In this paper, we present QWeaver, a task-graph-based programming and orchestration workflow framework for quantum circuit cutting that accepts OpenQASM quantum circuits as input and constructs a directed acyclic task graph. In this graph, the Multi-Level Intermediate Representation (MLIR)-based circuit cut is the first task, responsible for analyzing and partitioning the input circuit into executable fragment representations; the generated fragments are then handed to a set of quantum circuit execution tasks that depend on the cut task and can be dispatched concurrently across available quantum backends via the Quantum Intelligent Runtime System (Q-IRIS). Finally, a weaving task, dependent on all execution tasks, performs classical post-processing that applies quasi-probability reconstruction techniques to combine the sampled measurement outcomes of all fragments and recover an accurate approximation of the original circuit's output distribution. We describe the architecture of QWeaver, its integration with Q-IRIS and the execution engine for the Quantum Intermediate Representation (QIR-EE), validate end-to-end reconstruction on GHZ and Harris-Ross instances, and evaluate systems and width trade-offs on structured GHZ simulator workloads.
tldr: QWeaver is an end-to-end task-graph-based workflow for quantum circuit cutting, integrating MLIR-based partitioning, runtime orchestration, and classical reconstruction.
motivation: Current quantum devices have too few qubits and too much noise to execute large circuits directly, and while circuit cutting can partition circuits into smaller pieces, orchestrating the full workflow remains a major programming challenge.
method: The framework accepts OpenQASM circuits and builds a DAG task graph where an MLIR-based cut task partitions the circuit, execution tasks are dispatched concurrently via Q-IRIS/QIR-EE, and a final weaving task reconstructs results using quasi-probability techniques.
result: The authors validate end-to-end reconstruction on GHZ and Harris-Ross instances and evaluate systems and circuit-width trade-offs on structured GHZ simulator workloads.
conclusion: QWeaver provides a compiler-runtime orchestration framework for practical quantum circuit cutting, automating partitioning, execution, and post-processing for large circuits on constrained devices.

title: The Bapat-Sunder Eigenvalue Conjecture Fails Over The Reals
authors: Logan R. Chalmers
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1986 Bapat and Sunder asked whether [MATH] is the largest eigenvalue of [MATH] for every positive semidefinite Hermitian [MATH], where [MATH] deletes row [MATH] and column [MATH]. Drury disproved this over the complex field in 2018 and conjectured that the property holds for real positive semidefinite matrices. We disprove Drury's conjecture with a rank-[MATH], [MATH] integer Gram matrix and an integer vector whose Rayleigh quotient exceeds [MATH]; verification uses integer arithmetic. Together, the two counterexamples resolve the Bapat-Sunder eigenvalue conjecture negatively over both fields. Counterexamples exist of every order [MATH]. As an application to quantum optics, the violation yields a [MATH]-mode orthogonal interferometer and a direction of relative arrival-time delays among [MATH] photons with identical-variance Gaussian wave packets along which every sufficiently small nonzero delay increases the probability that all photons are detected within four designated output modes.
tldr: The paper disproves Drury's real-matrix version of the Bapat-Sunder eigenvalue conjecture using an integer Gram-matrix counterexample and notes a quantum-optics application involving photon arrival-time delays.
motivation: The Bapat-Sunder conjecture asked whether deleting a row and column of a positive semidefinite Hermitian matrix always lowers the largest eigenvalue; after a complex counterexample, the remaining question was whether the property might hold over the reals.
method: The author constructs a rank-deficient integer Gram matrix and an integer vector whose Rayleigh quotient exceeds the largest eigenvalue of the corresponding reduced matrix, verified with integer arithmetic; counterexamples are shown to exist in every order.
result: Drury's real positive semidefinite conjecture is false, resolving the Bapat-Sunder eigenvalue conjecture negatively over both complex and real fields; an application yields a multimode orthogonal interferometer and a direction of relative arrival-time delays among photons with identical-variance Gaussian wave packets.
conclusion: The work settles a matrix-analysis eigenvalue conjecture and provides a specialized quantum-optics consequence, but it is not primarily a quantum-information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems contribution.

title: Topological Signatures Of Criticality: The Ising Case
authors: Tak-Shing Chan, Pawe{\l} D{\l}otko, Jacek Gulgowski, Biagio Lucini, Mateusz Mas{\l}owski, Davide Vadacchino
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological properties of microscopic configurations may provide additional insight into phase transitions beyond conventional thermodynamic observables. We investigate this idea in the two-dimensional Ising model on square and triangular lattices by associating cell complexes with the positive and negative spin domains and constructing an Euler-characteristic observable from their difference. We provide the expression relating this quantity to conventional observables of the Ising model. This derivation allows us to understand its expected behavior physically. As a byproduct, we show that at any finite positive temperature the expectation of the Euler characteristic exceeds a positive, lattice-size-independent bound, hence disproving a previously suggested conjecture. Monte Carlo simulations combined with multihistogram reweighting show that this spin-odd topological observable exhibits order-parameter-like behavior near the ferromagnetic transition. Finite-size scaling of its susceptibility yields pseudocritical temperatures that converge to the known critical temperature for both lattice geometries. On the square lattice, the leading-order estimate of the critical exponent obtained from the topological observable depends more strongly on the fitting range than the magnetization estimate. This behavior is consistent with stronger subleading finite-size corrections, as supported by fits including an additional correction term. On the triangular lattice, the corresponding estimate remains consistent with the theoretical Ising value. Our study suggests that topologically defined quantities such as the Euler characteristic can provide an alternative way to locate order-disorder phase transitions in the systems considered here. Since the definition of these observables is purely geometrical, they can provide useful insights in cases in which order parameters cannot be constructed.
tldr: The paper introduces an Euler-characteristic-based topological observable built from spin-domain cell complexes to locate the ferromagnetic phase transition in the classical 2D Ising model on square and triangular lattices.
motivation: Conventional thermodynamic observables may miss topological fingerprints of phase transitions, so the authors ask whether purely geometric/topological quantities of microscopic configurations can serve as alternative order parameters, especially where order parameters cannot be constructed.
method: They associate cell complexes with positive and negative spin domains, define the difference of their Euler characteristics, derive its relation to standard Ising observables, and perform Monte Carlo simulations with multihistogram reweighting plus finite-size scaling of the susceptibility.
result: The spin-odd topological observable shows order-parameter-like behavior, its susceptibility pseudocritical temperatures converge to the known critical temperature on both lattices, and the critical-exponent estimate suffers stronger subleading corrections on the square lattice; they also disprove a previously conjectured lower-bound conjecture by showing a positive lattice-size-independent bound at finite temperature.
conclusion: Topologically defined quantities such as the Euler characteristic offer a viable geometric route to locating order-disorder transitions, potentially useful in systems lacking conventional order parameters.

title: Retained Encrypted Search With Certified Split Joins
authors: Liwen Ouyang Yavor Litchev
abstract: ArXiv:2611.24265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retaining encrypted search across data edits and worker replacement requires separating computational validity from current release authority. We give exact Hamming search with at most one authorized decryption and decoding attempt per query preparation. Under authenticated prescribed execution, exclusive nonrollback owner state, an ideal public seed-expansion interface and a stated observation model, we reduce bounded adaptive privacy to ordinary ring learning with errors (Ring-LWE). Expanded second components depend only on public masks and fixed maps, independently of queries and the fresh database key. This compiler invariant permits a retained split join against a smaller-modulus encrypted database. A simultaneous bound on the completed circuit covers a finite honest reservation family, including adaptive queries and slot selection, with explicit statistical correctness and privacy losses. In three post-calibration local CPU comparisons on 32,768 vectors of 512 bits, the 60-bit-join construction takes a median 9.825 s for an end-to-end two-query workload, versus 12.159 s for the optimized full-source-modulus baseline. These times include setup, transfers, preparation and private completion. They are local implementation results, not deployment or concrete-security claims.
tldr: The paper presents a cryptographic construction for retained encrypted search with certified split joins, reducing privacy to Ring-LWE under specified execution and observation assumptions.
motivation: Encrypted search systems need to remain secure and correct across data edits and worker replacement, motivating a design that separates computational validity from current release authority.
method: The authors give an exact Hamming-search protocol allowing at most one authorized decryption/decoding attempt per query preparation, using Ring-LWE-based privacy and a compiler invariant for retained split joins on a smaller-modulus encrypted database.
result: In local CPU comparisons on 32,768 vectors of 512 bits, the 60-bit-join construction has a median 9.825 s for a two-query end-to-end workload versus 12.159 s for the optimized full-source-modulus baseline.
conclusion: The work provides a bounded adaptive privacy reduction and an implementation-level performance comparison, but explicitly does not claim deployment or concrete security.

title: Norm Approximation With Linear Growth Of Error For Bosonic Dynamics In The Mean-Field Regime
authors: Niels Benedikter, Chiara Boccato, Umberto Morellini
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the quantum many-body dynamics of a homogeneous confined Bose gas in three dimensions in the mean-field scaling regime. We study the Cauchy problem for a class of initial data describing finitely many excitations over a Bose-Einstein condensate. Using a rigorous version of Bogolyubov's theory, we prove that the many-body evolution can be approximated in Fock space norm by a quasifree evolution of the excitations with an error which grows linearly in time. In distinction from earlier results, the slow growth in time holds even though the effective equation is not dispersive.
tldr: The paper proves a Fock-space norm approximation for the mean-field dynamics of a confined 3D Bose gas, with error growing only linearly in time and allowing non-dispersive effective dynamics.
motivation: Rigorous Bogolyubov theory has often yielded effective approximations whose error control depends on dispersive properties or short times; this work aims to extend validity to longer times without assuming dispersion.
method: The authors use a rigorous version of Bogolyubov's theory to compare the full many-body evolution of finitely many excitations over a condensate to a quasifree effective evolution in Fock space norm.
result: They obtain a norm approximation with an error that grows linearly in time, even though the effective equation is not dispersive, improving on earlier results requiring stronger assumptions.
conclusion: The result provides a rigorous long-time effective description of mean-field bosonic dynamics for a class of initial data with finitely many excitations, broadening the applicability of Bogolyubov theory.

title: In Situ Training Of Optical Neural Networks By Coding Agents
authors: Ilker Oguz, Colin Christian, Christophe Moser, Demetri Psaltis, Gordon Wetzstein
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical neural networks promise fast, energy-efficient computing, but every device departs from its design and must be trained with the hardware. In situ training relies on an expert-built calibrated digital model of each device or on gradient-free trial and error. Coding agents, large language models that write and run programs, have shown an emergent ability to understand and edit the weights of digital neural networks. Here we introduce optics as code, a method in which a coding agent trains an optical neural network from measurements alone, through a harness that returns camera images of its probes and requires a hypothesis per request. We discovered that the agent forms a physical understanding of the optics and reparametrizes the network with interpretable optical elements tuned on the hardware. It outperforms gradient-free methods in classification and image encoding, approaching backpropagation through a calibrated model at a fraction of the cost. Needing neither per-device calibration nor gradients through the hardware, and improving with more capable models, optics as code offers a practical route to large, scalable optical neural networks and a general tool for calibrating and optimizing optical experiments.
tldr: A coding-agent (LLM) framework called 'optics as code' trains optical neural networks directly on hardware from camera measurements alone, without per-device calibration or gradients through the hardware.
motivation: Optical neural networks offer fast, energy-efficient computing, but fabrication and alignment deviations mean each device must be trained in situ, which currently requires either an expert-built calibrated digital model or inefficient gradient-free search.
method: The authors give an LLM coding agent a harness that returns camera images of its optical probes and requires a hypothesis with each request; the agent then reparametrizes the network into interpretable optical elements tuned on the hardware.
result: The agent outperforms gradient-free methods on classification and image encoding, approaching backpropagation through a calibrated model at a fraction of the cost, and improves with stronger underlying models.
conclusion: Optics-as-code provides a practical, calibration-free route to scalable optical neural networks and a general tool for optimizing and calibrating optical experiments.

title: Data Poisoning Attacks To Locally Differentially Private Triangle Counting Protocols
authors: Tingxuan Han, Wei Tong, Zijian Wang, Sheng Zhong
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local differential privacy (LDP) has become a crucial paradigm for privacy-preserving graph analytics, enabling graph analytics tasks such as subgraph counting without requiring a trusted curator. However, while LDP provides strong privacy guarantees, the integrity and robustness of LDP subgraph counting protocols in the presence of malicious participants remain poorly understood. In particular, since data are randomized locally before collection, it is inherently difficult to distinguish malicious users from honest ones based solely on their submitted reports, and small, protocol-compliant local manipulations can be systematically amplified through reconstruction and calibration into large global estimation bias. In this paper, we use LDP triangle counting as a representative task to characterize the vulnerability of LDP subgraph counting to data poisoning attacks. For both non-interactive and interactive LDP triangle counting protocols, we analyze their attack surfaces and develop a unified gain-driven framework that captures how adversarial users can manipulate calibrated subgraph count estimates, which we instantiate on representative protocols of both types. Extensive experiments on four real-world graph datasets demonstrate that these attacks can significantly distort triangle count estimates across different protocols and adversarial settings. Moreover, we show that existing and straightforward defenses are insufficient to mitigate these attacks, underscoring the need for robustness mechanisms tailored to LDP subgraph counting.
tldr: This paper characterizes data poisoning attacks against locally differentially private (LDP) triangle counting protocols and shows that protocol-compliant malicious users can systematically inflate global estimation bias.
motivation: LDP provides strong privacy guarantees for graph analytics, but the integrity and robustness of LDP subgraph counting under malicious participants is poorly understood, since locally randomized reports are hard to distinguish from honest ones.
method: The authors analyze the attack surfaces of both non-interactive and interactive LDP triangle counting protocols and develop a unified gain-driven framework, instantiated on representative protocols, to model how adversarial users manipulate calibrated subgraph count estimates.
result: Experiments on four real-world graph datasets show the attacks significantly distort triangle count estimates across protocols and adversarial settings, and that existing straightforward defenses are insufficient.
conclusion: Robustness mechanisms tailored specifically to LDP subgraph counting are needed to defend against poisoning by malicious participants.

title: A Characterization Of Rings Where A Linear Transformation And Its Inverse And Transpose Have The Same Information Exchange
authors: Carlo Fantozzi Gianfranco Bilardi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.24099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear transformations are considered over finite commutative rings. It is shown that the information exchange of an invertible linear transformation and that of its inverse are equal for any ring. It is also shown that the information exchange of any linear transformation and that of its transpose are equal if and only if the ring is Frobenius. Applications are presented to the Discrete Fourier Transform, to the analysis of Vandermonde transformations, and to area-time complexity.
tldr: The paper characterizes finite commutative rings for which the information exchange of a linear transformation equals that of its transpose, proving equality always for inverses and characterizing transpose equality via Frobenius rings.
motivation: Information exchange is a measure of communication complexity for linear transformations, and understanding its symmetries under inverse and transpose is mathematically and computationally relevant.
method: The authors study invertible and general linear transformations over finite commutative rings, proving algebraic characterizations and applying them to discrete Fourier transforms, Vandermonde transformations, and area-time complexity.
result: Equality of information exchange for a transformation and its inverse holds over any ring, while equality for a transformation and its transpose holds exactly for Frobenius rings.
conclusion: The work provides a ring-theoretic characterization of symmetry properties of information exchange and demonstrates applications in transform analysis and complexity bounds.

title: Pivot: Distribution-Preserving Multi-BitWatermarking With Minimax-Optimal Scoring
authors: Wen Zhang, Kaiyi Pang, Minhao Bai, Shuyu Gan, Liping Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2611.24109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As LLM-generated content becomes increasingly widespread, reliable attribution calls for multi-bit watermarks that embed recoverable messages without distorting the output distribution. We introduce PIVOT, a multi-bit watermark with model-free verification based on mirrored rank-interval sampling. At each generation step, PIVOT uses a keyed pseudorandom scalar and a secret permutation of the vocabulary. The message bit determines whether next-token probability intervals are arranged in forward or reverse secret-rank order. Sampling from these mirrored layouts preserves every token probability exactly while inducing an opposite-signed dependence between the scalar and the sampled token's secret rank. This dependence yields a pivotal rank statistic whose null distribution is invariant to the unknown next-token law, enabling model-free calibration and decoding. We formulate joint watermark detection and message recovery as a multiple-hypothesis testing problem, derive a moment-robust minimax-optimal detection score over a relaxed moment class, and establish finite-sample recovery guarantees. Extensive experiments on two representative large language models validate the effectiveness of PIVOT, demonstrating reliable watermark detection and message recovery while preserving the generator's output distribution.
tldr: PIVOT is a multi-bit LLM watermarking scheme that preserves the output distribution and enables model-free detection and message recovery using mirrored rank-interval sampling and minimax-optimal scoring.
motivation: As LLM-generated content spreads, reliable attribution requires multi-bit watermarks that embed recoverable messages without distorting the model's output distribution.
method: The scheme uses keyed pseudorandom scalars and secret vocabulary permutations to arrange next-token probability intervals in forward or reverse order according to message bits, yielding a pivotal rank statistic with a null distribution invariant to the unknown token law; detection and recovery are framed as multiple-hypothesis testing.
result: The authors derive a moment-robust minimax-optimal detection score and finite-sample recovery guarantees, and experiments on two LLMs show reliable detection and message recovery while preserving the generator distribution.
conclusion: PIVOT provides a distribution-preserving, model-free multi-bit watermarking approach with strong theoretical and empirical performance, but it is outside the quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems scope.

title: The Double Entropy Fit Index (defi): An Information-Theoretic Approach To Dimensionality Reduction And Clustering
authors: Gabriel Lawrence (department Of Systems And Information Engineering, University Of Virginia), Daniel Otero-Leon
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23523v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the Double-Entropy Fit Index (DEFI), a regularized information-theoretic criterion for selecting among candidate graph partitions and reduced representations. DEFI couples entropy-based compression with relevance preservation and penalizes model dimensionality, cluster imbalance, and partition fragmentation. An exact R\'enyi-2 entropy identity shows that partitioning alters both spectral concentration and graph-volume normalization, explaining why unregularized entropy minimization can favor degenerate solutions. Across a 243-condition population-analytic factor recovery benchmark, DEFI achieved an overall exact recovery rate of 97.2\% (versus 75.0\% for EGA-TMFG, 45.8\% for TEFI on von Neumann entropy). In controlled local candidate batteries (distinguishing the true model from adjacent [MATH] and factor-split alternatives), DEFI identified the correct partition in 99.2\% of replications. Across ten clustering benchmarks, DEFI-guided Gaussian mixtures achieved a mean ARI of 0.929, exceeding HDBSCAN (0.809), Ward clustering (0.700), and conventional GMM criteria (0.501-0.580), with gains concentrating where standard criteria over-extract components.
tldr: The paper introduces DEFI, a regularized entropy-based criterion for selecting graph partitions and reduced representations in clustering and factor-recovery settings.
motivation: Unregularized entropy minimization in graph-partition-based dimensionality reduction can favor degenerate solutions, so a criterion is needed that balances compression with relevance preservation while penalizing model complexity and fragmentation.
method: DEFI combines Rényi-2 entropy-based compression, a relevance-preservation term, and penalties on dimensionality, cluster imbalance and fragmentation; an exact Rényi-2 entropy identity is derived to explain spectral and volume-normalization effects, and the index is benchmarked against EGA-TMFG, TEFI, HDBSCAN, Ward clustering and GMM criteria.
result: DEFI achieved 97.2% exact recovery in a 243-condition factor-recovery benchmark (vs 75.0% for EGA-TMFG and 45.8% for TEFI) and 99.2% correct identification in local candidate batteries, with a mean ARI of 0.929 across ten clustering benchmarks.
conclusion: DEFI is an effective regularized information-theoretic model-selection criterion for clustering and dimensionality reduction, outperforming standard alternatives especially where conventional criteria over-extract components.

title: Formalizing Local Gauge Freedom Via Bi-equivariant Groupoid Algebras
authors: Emil Prodan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gauge degrees of freedom appear in many different contexts. Here, we describe their emergence in the context of architected metamaterials built from self-coupling blocks with internal symmetries. Quantifying the dynamics requires choices of local frames and the many available options constitute the local gauge degrees of freedom of the problem. In the absence of internal symmetries, the dynamical matrices generating the dynamics are all built from the left regular representation of a groupoid C*-algebra canonically associated to the architecture. If the resonators display internal symmetries, we show that the mentioned groupoid C*-algebra accepts a natural 2-action by the group of internal symmetries and that the local gauge freedom can be encoded in a bi-equivariant sub-groupoid algebra generated from the mentioned 2-action. The latter is shown to be the smallest C*-algebra containing all dynamical matrices that can be engineered in a laboratory, for a given architecture and discrete group of internal symmetries.
tldr: The paper formalizes local gauge freedom in architected metamaterials using bi-equivariant groupoid C*-algebras.
motivation: Gauge degrees of freedom arise when local frames must be chosen to quantify dynamics in systems with internal symmetries.
method: It associates a groupoid C*-algebra to the architecture and encodes internal symmetries via a 2-action, yielding a bi-equivariant sub-groupoid algebra.
result: The constructed algebra is claimed to be the smallest C*-algebra containing all laboratory-engineerable dynamical matrices for a given architecture and discrete internal symmetry group.
conclusion: This provides a mathematical framework for gauge freedom in metamaterials but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Renormalization And Exact Bloch Bands: The Trigonometric Rosen-Morse Model
authors: H. G. Vianna Ulysses Camara Da Silva
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the trigonometric Rosen-Morse potential as an isolated singular well and as an exactly solvable periodic lattice. The potential combines inverse-square singularities with Coulomb terms of opposite signs. In the strongly attractive regime, independent renormalization at the two endpoints gives a two-parameter family of spectra. Deep negative-energy levels form two asymptotic sequences with the same Efimov-like scaling and opposite first-order Coulomb corrections. In the weak-medium regime, self-adjoint matching conditions allow transmission between neighboring cells. We obtain the exact Bloch dispersion relation and determine the band widths, gaps, and electron and hole effective masses. At fixed band index, the bandwidth becomes exponentially small in the limit of large Coulomb coupling.
tldr: The paper analyzes the trigonometric Rosen-Morse potential as an isolated singular well and as an exactly solvable periodic lattice, deriving renormalized spectra and exact Bloch bands.
motivation: The model combines inverse-square singularities with Coulomb terms and may serve as an exactly solvable lattice with tunable band structure.
method: The authors study endpoint renormalization in the strongly attractive regime and self-adjoint matching conditions in the weak-medium regime to obtain exact dispersion relations.
result: They find two Efimov-like asymptotic energy sequences, exact Bloch dispersion, band widths, gaps, effective masses, and exponentially small bandwidths at large Coulomb coupling.
conclusion: The trigonometric Rosen-Morse model provides an analytically tractable periodic lattice with controllable spectral and transport properties, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Observation Of Exact Mobility-Edge Phases In Two-Dimensional Photonic Quasicrystals
authors: Chaohua Wu, Yingying Shi, Juan Kang, Qinglong Zhang, Shuo Liu, Gang Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mobility edges, separating localized and extended states in energy, are central to localization physics. While exact mobility edges have been established in several one-dimensional quasiperiodic models, their realization in two dimensions remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover a general route to exact mobility edges in the two-dimensional Aubry-Andre quasicrystal by introducing auxiliary subsystems. Through isospectral reduction, we reveal a hidden self-dual structure that yields exact mobility-edge conditions, separating extended, localized, and partially localized states in the spectrum. Tailoring the auxiliary structures controls the effective couplings and resulting mobility edge configurations, while auxiliary resonances further support flat-band states. In a decorated Lieb-type quasicrystal, we experimentally realize these predicted phases in photonic waveguide lattices and probe their energy-dependent localization through site-selective quench dynamics. Our results provide a versatile platform for controlling localization and can be readily extended to other physical platforms and higher-dimensional systems.
tldr: The paper reports exact mobility-edge phases in two-dimensional photonic quasicrystals using auxiliary subsystems and waveguide-lattice experiments.
motivation: Mobility edges are central to localization physics, but exact mobility edges in two dimensions remain largely unexplored compared with one-dimensional quasiperiodic models.
method: The authors introduce auxiliary subsystems in a two-dimensional Aubry-Andre quasicrystal, use isospectral reduction to reveal a hidden self-dual structure, and experimentally probe the predicted phases in decorated Lieb-type photonic waveguide lattices via site-selective quench dynamics.
result: They obtain exact mobility-edge conditions separating extended, localized, and partially localized states, and show that auxiliary structures control effective couplings, mobility-edge configurations, and flat-band states.
conclusion: The work provides a versatile platform for controlling localization in two-dimensional quasicrystals and may extend to other physical platforms and higher-dimensional systems.

title: Hessian--Maslov Geometry Of Oja--Brockett Flows
authors: Shintaro Yoshizawa
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is organized in three parts. Part I develops the theoretical foundations of the Maslov index for caustics of the Legendre map, covering its semiclassical origin, geometric formulation as an intersection number in the Lagrangian Grassmannian, Hormander's local formula, and the dynamical viewpoint of bifurcating fixed points of a gradient flow. The theory is illustrated on the two-dimensional vector-valued quartic potential, whose caustic is a cusp and whose minima and saddles exchange stability when the eigenvalue ratio crosses 1. Part II lifts the setting to tall n x k matrices and introduces the potential f(X) = -1/2 tr(A^2 X B^2 X^T) + 1/4 tr[(A X B X^T)^2]. Numerical evidence confirms that fixed points of the associated negative gradient flow realize Brockett's sorting theorem. When eigenvalues of A or B degenerate, the fixed-point set expands into a flag manifold; crossing a Weyl wall produces Hessian degeneracy and an exchange of sort order. These phenomena are identified with the Maslov cycle, showing that combinatorial inversion numbers (Coxeter length) and the differential-geometric Maslov index are two faces of the same wall-crossing. Part III supplies the rigorous analysis underlying Part II. The ambient Hessian of the general Oja-Brockett flow dot{X} = A X B - X B X^T A X is completely decomposed into normal, vertical and horizontal sectors, and closed spectral formulas depending on both SPD matrices A and B are derived. In particular, the formula mu^V_{ij} = (lambda_i - lambda_j)(b_i - b_j) reveals a second, dual wall system (the B-wall) that is independent of the classical Weyl wall of A. Under this double-wall structure a genuine eigenvalue crossing becomes an avoided crossing; the associated horizontal and vertical coupling constants are given in closed form.
tldr: The paper develops Maslov-index and Hessian geometry for Oja-Brockett gradient flows, linking caustics, Weyl-wall crossings, flag manifolds, and Brockett sorting.
motivation: It aims to unify semiclassical Maslov theory, Lagrangian geometry, and matrix sorting dynamics through the Oja-Brockett flow.
method: It combines geometric formulation of the Maslov index, explicit potentials for tall matrices, numerical evidence, and spectral decomposition of the ambient Hessian into normal, vertical, and horizontal sectors.
result: The flow recovers Brockett sorting at nondegenerate fixed points, while eigenvalue degeneracies expand fixed-point sets to flag manifolds and produce dual A- and B-wall systems with avoided crossings.
conclusion: Combinatorial inversion numbers and the differential-geometric Maslov index are shown to describe the same wall-crossing phenomenon in this matrix-flow setting.

title: Existence Of Srb Measures For Some R\"ossler Systems
authors: Th\'eophile Caby
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for the R\"ossler system [MATH], [MATH], [MATH] with [MATH], the set of parameters [MATH] within [MATH] of the classical value [MATH] for which the flow has a H\'enon-like strange attractor supporting a Sinai--Ruelle--Bowen (SRB) measure has positive Lebesgue measure. The key step, proved with computer assistance, is that at a parameter localised in an explicit interval within [MATH] of [MATH] the period-one saddle of the Poincar\'e map has a quadratic homoclinic tangency that unfolds generically; the conclusion then follows from the theorems of Mora--Viana, Benedicks--Young and Benedicks--Viana. The same method gives two further such tangencies near [MATH] and one at the band-merging parameter [MATH]. The proof reduces the generic-tangency conditions to finitely many inequalities, through explicit [MATH] graph-transform bounds for the local invariant manifolds of a Poincar\'e map whose area contraction is of order [MATH]--[MATH], and a scalar tangency function. The inequalities are checked with interval arithmetic in CAPD and re-checked with an independent implementation based on the Kv library; the analytic tangency criterion is formalised in Lean~4. Whether an SRB measure exists at [MATH] itself remains open.
tldr: The paper proves that for the classical Rössler system, a positive-measure set of parameters near the classical value yields Hénon-like strange attractors supporting SRB measures, verified via computer-assisted interval arithmetic.
motivation: Whether the Rössler flow possesses a Sinai–Ruelle–Bowen measure at or near its classical parameter values has remained an open problem in the theory of chaotic dynamical systems.
method: The authors establish, with computer assistance, a generic quadratic homoclinic tangency of the period-one saddle of the Poincaré map, reducing the genericity conditions to finitely many inequalities checked by interval arithmetic in CAPD and the Kv library, with the analytic criterion formalised in Lean 4.
result: Positive Lebesgue measure of parameters within a small neighbourhood of the classical value admit Hénon-like strange attractors with SRB measures, and further tangencies are found near zero and at the band-merging parameter.
conclusion: The results extend Mora–Viana, Benedicks–Young and Benedicks–Viana theorems to the Rössler system, though existence of an SRB measure at the classical parameter itself remains open.

title: Conditional Limit Theorems In Dynamical Systems
authors: Jason Atnip, Gary Froyland, Cecilia Gonz\'alez-Tokman, Yushi Nakano, Sandro Vaienti
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a comprehensive theory of conditional limit theorems for open dynamical systems. We study the statistical properties of the dynamics within transient regimes by establishing a suite of limit theorems describing the behavior of trajectories under the condition that they remain outside a ``hole'', or region of no return. Under a spectral gap assumption for the associated open transfer operator, we first establish conditioning and Yaglom limits and identify the corresponding conditionally invariant and conditionally ergodic measures. We then establish conditional exponential decay of correlations and the Strong Law of Large Numbers for both deterministic and quenched random systems. We also obtain a conditional Central Limit Theorem, Large Deviation Principle, and Berry--Esseen theorem, with additional assumptions in the quenched random case. We also derive standard (non-conditional) limit theorems on the surviving set of points that never enter the hole.
tldr: The paper builds a general theory of conditional limit theorems for open dynamical systems whose trajectories are conditioned to avoid a hole, deriving Yaglom limits, decay of correlations, CLTs, LDPs, and Berry-Esseen bounds.
motivation: Transient dynamics in open systems with a region of no return are poorly captured by standard ergodic-theoretic limit theorems, motivating a systematic conditional theory of survival statistics.
method: Under a spectral gap assumption on the open transfer operator, the authors establish conditioning and Yaglom limits, identify conditionally invariant and conditionally ergodic measures, and extend results to quenched random systems.
result: They obtain conditional exponential decay of correlations, a Strong Law of Large Numbers, a conditional Central Limit Theorem, a Large Deviation Principle, and a Berry-Esseen theorem, plus standard limit theorems on the surviving set.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive framework for statistical properties of surviving trajectories in deterministic and random open dynamical systems.

title: The Geometry Of Mode Sampling In Reconfigurable Mimo Channel Extrapolation
authors: Chongwen Huang Shaoyang Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pattern-reconfigurable arrays acquire channels by distributing radiation modes across their antenna elements. Equal mode counts fix the observation budget while leaving a spatial sampling choice that directly affects reconstruction of unmeasured channels. We establish how this assignment enters the inverse problem through the receive aperture and the coupling between propagation paths. For an isolated path with calibrated positive real responses, the power-weighted variance of antenna positions completely characterizes the assignment dependence of the profiled angle information at fixed mode counts. We then construct layouts with identical weighted apertures and different path correlations, exposing a limitation of aperture-based design in multipath propagation. A paired simulation study evaluates balanced random, contiguous, interleaved, and equal-moment sampling using a common estimator with per-detection joint angle refinement. Balanced random sampling substantially reduces complete-channel error relative to ascending contiguous blocks when some modes are entirely unobserved, with improvements across nearly all tested scenes at high signal-to-noise ratio. When every mode is sampled, the mean benefit is more sensitive to rare large errors. Together, the analysis and experiments connect the spatial distribution of mode measurements to both extrapolation accuracy and reconstruction stability.
tldr: The paper analyzes how spatial mode-sampling layouts in reconfigurable MIMO arrays affect channel extrapolation accuracy and reconstruction stability.
motivation: Pattern-reconfigurable arrays can observe only a fixed number of radiation modes, so the assignment of modes to antenna elements creates a spatial sampling design problem for reconstructing unmeasured channels.
method: The authors formulate the mode-assignment dependence through the receive aperture and path coupling, characterize isolated-path angle information via the power-weighted variance of antenna positions, and compare balanced random, contiguous, interleaved, and equal-moment sampling layouts in paired simulations.
result: Balanced random sampling substantially reduces complete-channel error relative to ascending contiguous blocks when some modes are unobserved, especially at high SNR, while equal weighted apertures can still yield different multipath performance.
conclusion: The spatial distribution of mode measurements directly affects both extrapolation accuracy and reconstruction stability, exposing limitations of aperture-only design in multipath propagation.

title: A Probabilistic Behavioral Rtl Simulation Framework For Probabilistic Compute Fabrics
authors: Zehuan Wang, Chaohui Li, Ruihong Yin, Xunqi Li, Chris H. Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coupled oscillator Ising hardware can produce different solution qualities across repeated runs of the same problem, while a deterministic behavioral model used for the design yields a single outcome under fixed conditions. Capturing this stochastic variability during design time is essential for evaluating how closely simulation reflects silicon behavior. This work presents a probabilistic behavioral RTL simulation framework that introduces Gaussian timing variation into coupling delays. This variation changes oscillator timing during evolution, producing different outcomes across runs while retaining the existing chip control and readout blocks. The framework is evaluated against measurements from two chips: a 28-nm CMOS chip with 66 spins and a 16-nm FinFET chip with 49 spins, using 250 problems run 100 times repetitively. Compared with deterministic simulation, the model reduces the average absolute gap between sorted simulation and silicon outcomes by 14.0% and 28.4% on the two chips, respectively. These results demonstrate that a simple behavioral timing variation model can be a useful tool for designing and verifying probabilistic computing chips.
tldr: The authors build a probabilistic behavioral RTL simulation framework that injects Gaussian timing variation into coupling delays of coupled-oscillator Ising hardware, so simulated runs reproduce the run-to-run solution variability seen on real chips.
motivation: Deterministic behavioral models of probabilistic computing fabrics yield a single outcome under fixed conditions, whereas silicon produces a distribution of solution qualities across repeated runs; design-time tools must capture this stochasticity to predict hardware behavior.
method: Gaussian timing variation is added to coupling delays in an RTL-level behavioral model, altering oscillator timing during evolution while reusing the existing chip control and readout blocks; the framework is validated against measurements from a 28-nm CMOS 66-spin chip and a 16-nm FinFET 49-spin chip over 250 problems each repeated 100 times.
result: Relative to deterministic simulation, the probabilistic model reduces the average absolute gap between sorted simulated and measured silicon outcomes by 14.0% and 28.4% on the two chips respectively.
conclusion: A simple behavioral timing-variation model is a practical tool for designing and verifying probabilistic computing chips, though it remains an engineering/design-automation contribution rather than a physics or information-theoretic one.

title: From A Finite Subgroup Of $so(3)$:$c_2$ Leads To A Holant Dichotomy
authors: Yuxuan Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2611.24236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Counting complexity within the Holant framework has been extensively studied through complexity dichotomy theorems. While substantial progress has been achieved for various restricted settings, the general complex-valued even-arity case without auxiliary unary signatures remains largely open. This paper studies a fundamental case in this program where the binary signatures induce a group structure satisfying \(M(B())\cong C_2\). It is observed that projective equivalence classes of binary signature matrices naturally embed into finite subgroups of \(SO(3)\), providing an algebraic viewpoint for structural classification. This paper further identifies two fundamentally different regimes for the \(C_2\) case, namely the normal and isotropic cases, and analyzes their complexity behavior separately. Combining gadget constructions, decomposition techniques, interpolation arguments, and a realnumberization approach that transforms the complex-valued setting into an equivalent real-structured framework, this paper establishes a complete dichotomy theorem: for every even-arity signature set \(\) satisfying \(M(\B())\cong C_2\), the problem \(()\) is either polynomial-time computable or \#P-hard. A Pauli-basis representation for signatures is further introduced as an algebraically natural language for organizing realizable signatures and revealing structural relations that are less transparent in the standard basis.
tldr: The paper establishes a Holant dichotomy theorem for complex-valued even-arity binary signatures whose induced matrix group is isomorphic to C2.
motivation: Holant counting complexity has many dichotomy results, but the general complex-valued even-arity case without auxiliary unary signatures remains largely open.
method: It embeds projective equivalence classes of binary signature matrices into finite subgroups of SO(3), splits the C2 case into normal and isotropic regimes, and combines gadget constructions, decomposition, interpolation, and a realnumberization technique.
result: For every even-arity signature set satisfying M(B()) ≅ C2, the associated Holant problem is shown to be either polynomial-time computable or #P-hard.
conclusion: The work gives a complete dichotomy for this C2 case and introduces a Pauli-basis representation to organize realizable signatures and expose structural relations.

title: Pmkpir: Parallel Multi-Keyword Pir With Interleaved Batching For Private Boolean Retrieval
authors: Rongxi Wang, Guanxiong Ha, Chunfu Jia, Minfen Gao, Hanmiaomiao Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2611.24248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Keyword Private Information Retrieval (Keyword PIR) allows users to retrieve data associated with specific keywords from a database while protecting query privacy. However, existing Keyword PIR schemes supporting boolean retrieval either incur high computational overhead due to multiple database traversals, or fail to support universal boolean computation. We propose PMKPIR, a novel keyword PIR scheme supporting both parallel multi-keyword queries and universal boolean computation. We utilize the single instruction multiple data (SIMD) capability of BFV homomorphic encryption to propose an interleaved batching method, and design IBPIR based on this method, achieving the private matching of multiple keywords in a single database traversal. Furthermore, we design a boolean query processing method, extending the parallel capability of interleaved batching from keyword querying to boolean query computation, to support universal boolean computation and accelerate boolean operations. Building upon IBPIR, we integrate this method to further design PMKPIR. To the best of our knowledge, PMKPIR is the first Keyword PIR scheme to support multi-keyword batch matching within boolean queries. Security analysis demonstrates that, consistent with existing PIR schemes supporting boolean retrieval, PMKPIR preserves the core security guarantees of classic PIR. Compared with state-of-the-art schemes, PMKPIR reduces query time, communication overhead, storage overhead, and peak memory by up to 79.06%, 75.00%, 97.92%, and 80.26%, respectively.
tldr: PMKPIR is a keyword private information retrieval scheme built on BFV homomorphic encryption that supports parallel multi-keyword matching and universal boolean retrieval in a single database traversal.
motivation: Existing keyword PIR schemes with boolean retrieval either require multiple costly database traversals or cannot express universal boolean queries, limiting practical private retrieval.
method: The authors exploit BFV's SIMD packing to design an interleaved batching method and the IBPIR primitive, then extend batching to boolean query processing to build PMKPIR.
result: Compared with state-of-the-art schemes, PMKPIR reportedly reduces query time, communication, storage, and peak memory by up to 79.06%, 75.00%, 97.92%, and 80.26% respectively.
conclusion: PMKPIR is claimed to be the first keyword PIR scheme supporting multi-keyword batch matching within boolean queries while preserving classic PIR security guarantees.

title: Rational V. Radical: Trajectory Properties Of Iterated Bayesian Updates
authors: Clive Cenxin Aw, Lynette Zhong Ling Wang, Peter Sidajaya
abstract: ArXiv:2611.24430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Iterating Jeffrey's update on fixed evidence gives a maximum-likelihood estimate under suitable support conditions. What is less clear would be how the trajectories are organized, and what happens when we trace them in reverse. For a fixed strictly positive, invertible classical channel and full-support evidence, reverse iteration corresponds to repeated prior hacking. Almost every interior prior then approaches certainty in one possibility while each nontrivial step worsens agreement with the evidence. We call this limiting behavior radicalization. Priors that approach the same pure state form a Bayes phase. In the phase diagrams, the separating trajectories instead approach facet fixed points determined by M-projections. We also ask whether one can choose evidence that brings every interior prior to the same conclusion. For a strictly positive, invertible channel this is always possible, although one cannot always prescribe which conclusion it will be.
tldr: The paper analyzes trajectory properties of iterated Bayesian/Jeffrey updates on classical channels, introducing Bayes phases and radicalization under reverse iteration.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how repeated Bayesian updates organize over time and what happens when the update process is run backward, especially in terms of convergence to certainty and evidence agreement.
method: They study iterated Jeffrey updates for fixed strictly positive invertible classical channels and full-support evidence, analyzing forward and reverse trajectories, fixed points, M-projections, and phase diagrams.
result: Reverse iteration corresponds to repeated prior hacking, with almost every interior prior approaching certainty in one possibility while agreement with evidence worsens; priors reaching the same pure state form Bayes phases, and separating trajectories approach facet fixed points.
conclusion: For strictly positive invertible channels, evidence can always be chosen to bring every interior prior to the same conclusion, though the specific conclusion cannot always be prescribed.

title: Riesz And Lusin Type Theorems In Choquet Integral Spaces: Quasicontinuity And Density Of Continuous Functions For Monotone Measures
authors: Kiet Ho, Duc Toan Truong, Thanh Ngo Vo Ke, Cuong Le Quoc, Tran Nhat Luan
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the approximation of measurable functions by continuous functions, in measure and with respect to the Choquet, Sugeno and Shilkret integrals, for monotone measures on metric spaces. For every monotone measure, quasicontinuous functions are limits of continuous functions in measure and in the Sugeno integral; for unbounded Choquet integrable functions this remains true under a small-set subadditivity condition or under null-additivity. Conversely, under property [S1] and an outer smallness condition, every such limit is quasicontinuous, and examples show that neither condition can be omitted. This extends to monotone measures a classical description of the closure of continuous functions in capacitary [MATH]-spaces. We characterize the indicator functions in this closure by a symmetric approximation property of sets, and we give criteria, involving regularity and order continuity, for the density of bounded continuous functions. As applications, we show that two approximation theorems of Cao with compactly supported functions fail on spaces which are not locally compact, we prove that, for a given finite, continuous, weakly null-additive measure on a separable metric space, their conclusions for convergence in measure, for the Sugeno integral and for the Choquet integral of bounded functions hold if and only if the measure is concentrated on the set of points having a compact neighbourhood (and, under null-additivity, also for unbounded Choquet integrable functions), and we prove corrected versions on locally compact spaces; we describe the closure explicitly for possibility measures; and we give a Lebesgue-null Cantor dust which shows, for all [MATH] and [MATH], that continuous functions are not dense in the Choquet space of the dyadic Hausdorff content.
tldr: The paper proves Riesz- and Lusin-type approximation theorems for measurable functions by continuous functions in Choquet, Sugeno, and Shilkret integral spaces for monotone measures on metric spaces.
motivation: The authors aim to extend classical descriptions of the closure of continuous functions in capacitary spaces to the setting of monotone measures and non-additive integrals.
method: They study convergence in measure and approximation by continuous functions, characterize quasicontinuous functions and indicator functions in the closure, and give density criteria involving regularity and order continuity.
result: They establish quasicontinuity-limit equivalences under small-set subadditivity or null-additivity, provide counterexamples showing necessary conditions, characterize density of bounded continuous functions, and apply the results to correct and extend Cao's approximation theorems.
conclusion: The work clarifies when continuous functions are dense in Choquet-type spaces for monotone measures and provides explicit applications, including possibility measures and a Cantor dust example for dyadic Hausdorff content.

title: Digital Twin Models For Malaria Transmission: A Classical And Stieltjes Derivative Approach
authors: Iv\'an Area, Emmanuel Afolabi Bakare, Francisco J. Fern\'andez, Daniel Muyiwa Adefisoye
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose two mathematical models for malaria transmission grounded in mosquito--human interactions and the digital twin framework. The first model is formulated using classical derivatives, whereas the second employs Stieltjes derivatives to represent abrupt biological events such as egg hatching and adult-emergence pulses in mosquito populations. The Stieltjes formulation unifies, in a single equation with two derivators, the continuous transmission dynamics, the biological impulses and the data-assimilation corrections of the digital twin; we prove its well-posedness, specify the order of biological and assimilation atoms when they coincide, and give quantitative conditions under which additive emergence pulses preserve biological admissibility. The numerical study uses 132 monthly confirmed-malaria observations from Kebbi State (January 2015--December 2025) and a synthetic entomological series generated in a controlled recovery experiment, because no measured mosquito time series is available. Parameters are updated incrementally on rolling windows, and one-step-ahead forecasts combine the mechanistic ensemble with a past-only seasonal-persistence component. In the recovery experiment, the model endowed with seasonal recruitment and emergence pulses, which the Stieltjes derivator represents exactly, recovers the synthetic vector dynamics far better than the unforced classical model; this gain is attributable to the seasonal and impulsive mechanisms rather than to the derivative calculus itself, and the phase and pulse schedule of the generator were known to the model. The human-case results are comparable between both formulations; the one-step forecasts improve on a seasonal-naive predictor but not on last-month persistence, so they must be interpreted as a proof of concept rather than as an independent epidemiological validation.
tldr: The paper develops two malaria transmission models—one with classical derivatives and one with Stieltjes derivatives—within a digital twin framework, calibrated on monthly confirmed malaria cases from Kebbi State.
motivation: The authors aim to capture abrupt biological events such as egg hatching and adult-mosquito emergence pulses that classical derivative models cannot represent, while integrating real-time data assimilation for epidemiological forecasting.
method: A classical ODE model and a Stieltjes-derivative formulation with two derivators are constructed; well-posedness and admissibility conditions for additive emergence pulses are proven, and parameters are updated incrementally on rolling windows with one-step-ahead forecasts combining a mechanistic ensemble and seasonal persistence.
result: In a synthetic recovery experiment, the model with seasonal recruitment and emergence pulses recovers vector dynamics far better than the unforced classical model, though this gain stems from the seasonal/impulsive mechanisms rather than the derivative calculus; human-case forecasts improve on seasonal-naive but not on last-month persistence.
conclusion: The Stieltjes formulation offers a unified framework for continuous transmission, biological impulses, and data assimilation, but the human-case results remain a proof of concept rather than an independent epidemiological validation.

title: How Random Are Affine Maps Over Finite Cyclic Groups And Generalized Cyclotomic Permutations Over Finite Fields?
authors: Hugo Teixeira
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the dynamical behavior of affine permutations over the ring [MATH] and generalized cyclotomic permutations (GCPs) over the finite field [MATH]. We use the description of their functional graphs to determine two statistical parameters: the expected number of cycles and the expected length of a cycle that contains a random element. We obtain explicit closed-form expressions for both expectations and an exact reduction from GCPs to affine permutations. We compare these parameters with the corresponding expectations for random permutations, to determine how closely the cycle statistics of each family resemble those of random permutations.
tldr: The paper computes expected cycle counts and expected cycle lengths for affine permutations over Z_M and generalized cyclotomic permutations over finite fields, comparing them to random permutations.
motivation: Permutation families such as affine and cyclotomic permutations are used in cryptography and coding, so understanding how closely their cycle structure mimics that of random permutations is of practical interest.
method: Functional graph descriptions of the permutations are used to derive explicit closed-form expressions for the expected number of cycles and the expected cycle length of a random element, along with an exact reduction of GCPs to affine permutations.
result: Closed-form expectations are obtained for both families and compared quantitatively with the corresponding values for uniformly random permutations.
conclusion: The cycle statistics of these algebraic permutation families deviate from (or approximate) those of random permutations in a way that is now explicitly quantified.

title: Persistent Hydration And Ionic Mobility: When The Ion Is Not The Only Transported Species
authors: Biman Bagchi
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small-ion transport in water remains only partially understood despite more than a century of theoretical work. The difficulty is especially acute for strongly hydrated ions such as Li[MATH], Mg[MATH], and Ca[MATH], whose first hydration shells can persist on timescales comparable to or longer than translational motion. We develop a molecular framework in which the ion, its first hydration shell, and the outer solvent are treated as dynamically coupled components. Local hydration structure and exchange are represented through a potential of mean force and coordination dynamics, while collective solvent response is described through molecular memory functions. The theory clarifies why hydration cannot generally be represented by an additive friction or a single enlarged radius, and provides a route beyond conventional continuum and molecular descriptions.
tldr: A theoretical molecular framework treating a strongly hydrated ion, its first hydration shell, and the surrounding solvent as dynamically coupled components to explain persistent hydration and ionic mobility in water.
motivation: Small-ion transport in water, especially for strongly hydrated ions like Li+, Mg2+, and Ca2+, is poorly captured by continuum or simple molecular models because hydration shells can persist longer than translational motion.
method: The ion, first hydration shell, and outer solvent are modeled as coupled components, with local hydration structure and exchange described by a potential of mean force and coordination dynamics, and collective solvent response described by molecular memory functions.
result: The theory shows that hydration cannot be represented by additive friction or a single enlarged radius, and it provides a route beyond conventional continuum and molecular descriptions.
conclusion: Persistent hydration and the coupled dynamics of ion plus shell require a non-additive, memory-function-based treatment to correctly describe ionic mobility in water.

title: Simultaneous Spectral Measurement And Programmable Filtering On A Universal Silicon Photonic Chip
authors: Yangyang Wan, Rui Tang, Kazuhiro Ikeda, Makoto Okano, Kasidit Toprasertpong, Mitsuru Takenaka
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectral measurement and spectral filtering are two fundamental operations in optics, yet they are conventionally implemented using separate optical systems, hindering their simultaneous and programmable operation on a common platform. Here, we demonstrate a universal silicon photonic chip that unifies spectral measurement and programmable filtering within a single integrated architecture. The chip comprises two 8 * 8 programmable unitary transformation circuits interconnected through optical intensity modulators, forming a universal linear optical circuit. In contrast to conventional universal circuits employing equal-length interconnections, we deliberately introduce different optical path lengths between the two unitary circuits. The resulting wavelength-dependent phase evolution provides spectral diversity while preserving the programmability of the universal circuit, enabling parallel spectral measurement and programmable filtering. The fabricated chip achieves a spectral resolution of 0.05 nm over a bandwidth exceeding 100 nm, simultaneously measures eight independent laser sources, and generates multiple programmable spectral filter functions. We further demonstrate simultaneous spectral measurement and filtering during dynamic reconfiguration of the filter functions. These results establish universal photonic circuits as a versatile platform for integrating spectral sensing and programmable optical processing on a single chip.
tldr: A silicon photonic chip integrates spectral measurement and programmable filtering using two 8×8 programmable unitary circuits with unequal path lengths to create wavelength-dependent phase diversity.
motivation: Spectral measurement and filtering are typically performed by separate optical systems, motivating a single programmable platform that can perform both operations simultaneously.
method: The chip uses two interconnected 8×8 programmable unitary transformation circuits with intensity modulators and deliberately unequal optical path lengths to introduce spectral diversity while retaining programmability.
result: The fabricated chip achieves 0.05 nm spectral resolution over >100 nm bandwidth, measures eight independent laser sources simultaneously, and generates multiple programmable filter functions during dynamic reconfiguration.
conclusion: Universal silicon photonic circuits can serve as a versatile platform for integrated spectral sensing and programmable optical processing.

title: Charged Schr\"odinger Blocks In $1+1$ Dimensions From The Quartic Casimir And Endpoint Equations
authors: Hirohiko Shimada
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct charge-two Schr\"odinger conformal blocks in one spatial dimension, independently of any dynamical realization. We consider ordered vacuum four-point functions of fundamental fields of dimension [MATH], with homogeneous Schr\"odinger equations at the earliest and latest insertions and interactions allowed in the intermediate two-particle interval. For reduced blocks analytic in signed spatial coordinates and even under simultaneous spatial inversion, two functions of the time cross-ratio determine the full spatial dependence: the collinear value and a rescaled mixed spatial derivative. An exact Kummer lift, built from confluent hypergeometric functions, gives this reconstruction. An operator identity reduces the quartic Casimir equation, modulo the endpoint equations, to an equivalent coupled system for this pair. At generic exchanged dimension, OPE conditions select a unique block up to normalization for each primary parity. We obtain collinear [MATH] functions and sums of Kummer products, including the shadow branches. The blocks depend on the relative sign of the signed coordinates, distinguishing piecewise linear worldlines with an inflection from those with monotone segment velocities. In the Calogero model, we recover the previously derived bosonic four-point function and obtain its fermionic counterpart, with an independent integral check. At the diffusion-limited fixed point of [MATH], two blocks of opposite primary parity give the same collinear unlike-species response. Nonnegativity for all positions and ordered times selects the even family, thereby establishing that the response summed over species contains the even shadow pair with dimensions [MATH]. The nonnegativity argument demonstrates a concrete constraint for a Schr\"odinger bootstrap beyond collinear data.
tldr: The paper constructs charged Schrödinger conformal blocks in 1+1 dimensions using quartic Casimir and endpoint equations, with applications to Calogero-model four-point functions and a nonnegativity constraint for Schrödinger bootstrap.
motivation: The work aims to develop a bootstrap-style understanding of Schrödinger conformal blocks independently of dynamical realizations, extending constraints beyond collinear data.
method: It analyzes ordered vacuum four-point functions of charged fundamental fields, reduces the quartic Casimir equation modulo endpoint equations to a coupled system, and uses a Kummer lift via confluent hypergeometric functions to reconstruct spatial dependence.
result: At generic exchanged dimension, OPE conditions fix a unique block up to normalization for each primary parity; the Calogero bosonic four-point function is recovered and its fermionic counterpart obtained, and nonnegativity selects the even family in a diffusion-limited fixed point.
conclusion: The construction provides explicit Schrödinger blocks and a concrete nonnegativity constraint relevant to a Schrödinger bootstrap beyond collinear data, but it is unrelated to the specified quantum-information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems directions.

title: Spectral Dimension Reduction Of Dynamical Systems On Graphons
authors: Bisna Mary Eldo Naoki Masuda
abstract: ArXiv:2611.23238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectral dimension reduction approximates a dynamical system on a large network by a low-dimensional system whose variables are weighted averages of the node states, with weights given by dominant eigenvectors of the network. Its effectiveness is closely related to the low-rank structure of the interaction matrix. We develop a graphon analogue of this reduction for dynamical systems on dense graph limits. For graphon dynamical systems, we formulate the reduction in terms of the compact self-adjoint integral operator associated with the graphon.
